thread:
sarah (support): FYI customer AtlasWave via Okta SSO says their new org shows no API keys in their project, but they can hit the API with the key we created. 😕

maria (onboarding): Can you paste the org id and a screenshot? I want to confirm which project they're viewing.

sarah (support): Org id: org_azwf_12, console screenshot attached (link: https://redwood.internal/attachments/3987654321/atlaswave-console.png). They report: 'No keys in Project "atlaswave-prod"' but their app gets 200 using key XXXXXX (we redacted).

ops (infra): I pulled the provisioner logs for the time of onboarding (2026-03-15T10:02:03Z). Provisioner created key id key_8b9 and bound it to project id rw-internal-provisioning. Claim token: claim-789. Logs: ```INFO claim received claim-789 for org org_azwf_12
INFO created key key_8b9
INFO bound key_8b9 -> project rw-internal-provisioning (policy mismatch)
```

maria (onboarding): Hmm. That sounds like the claim was processed before the Okta assertion for org/project mapping finished. We're seeing an OIDC/SAML attribute race where the provisioner falls back to a default project.

tim (platform): Agreed. The fallback is `rw-internal-provisioning` when project lookup fails. Two fixes: 1) rebind existing key to customer's project; 2) harden provisioner to queue claim briefly (50-150ms) when mapping data is missing. For the immediate customer, rebind is needed.

sarah (support): Customer is asking for quick fix. What's the safe rebind command?

ops (infra): You can run: ```rbac-rebind --key-id key_8b9 --from-project rw-internal-provisioning --to-project atlaswave-prod --actor automated-reconcile``` Should be safe; it updates IAM bindings and project metadata atomically.

maria (onboarding): Before rebind, confirm the key fingerprint matches what customer is calling. Send them a 6-digit fingerprint suffix to validate.

sarah (support): Sent to customer: "Can you confirm the key ends with ...3f7a?" They confirmed yes. :thumbsup: 

ops (infra): I'll queue the rebind now. Note: rebind will trigger a short propagation window (~30s) where console views might be stale.

deploy-bot: ACTION triggered: rbac-rebind job_id=job_442 started by ops (infra) at 2026-03-15T10:12:11Z

ops (infra): Rebind completed. Job job_442 -> success. Post-rebind checks: key_8b9 now shows under project atlaswave-prod in metadata service; IAM policy updated.

sarah (support): Customer confirmed they can see the key in console and that calls still succeed. They report console now shows key under atlaswave-prod. :tada: 

maria (onboarding): Follow-up: adding a short guard to the provisioner to hold claim processing up to 200ms if project mapping is unresolved, and flagging SSO flows where mapping latency >100ms. I'll file a ticket.

ops (infra): Ticket created: PROV-1124 "Provisioner guard for SSO mapping race" with proposed fix and canary config.

maria (onboarding): Also scheduling an async job to scan recent 24h provisioner binds to detect other keys bound to rw-internal-provisioning that look like they should belong to external orgs.

sarah (support): Closing loop with customer and leaving note on their org: "Manual rebind performed 2026-03-15; root cause SSO mapping race; monitoring and fix in flight."

tim (platform): Nice. Please add the repro steps into PROV-1124: reproduce with delayed SAML attribute echo (we use `okta-simulate --delay-mapping 150ms`).

sarah (support): Will do. Closing thread.
